title: Fuzzy org match (difflib 0.9, ignores level) merges different schools and invents cross-school edges
detail: OrgIndex.resolve falls back to difflib.get_close_matches(n_state, all aliases, cutoff=0.9) for any NCAA/unknown level or any name containing university/college. It never checks that the matched org's level or state agrees with the stint. One-letter differences like Southern/Northern, Becker/Eckerd, Wesley/Wellesley, Taylor/Baylor, Iowa/Ohio Wesleyan and Tenn/Minn state hints all clear 0.9. In the real data 19 of the 21 fuzzy (raw, level) matches are wrong, covering 56 stints and 18 distinct raw names. Coaches from two schools are then joined into one org and get tree edges with each other: Peter Jennings (Iowa Wesleyan HC 2009) worked_under-mentors Pat Delaney (Ohio Wesleyan). Mike Deitrick (Allegany College of Maryland) worked_under B.J. Hammer at Allegheny 2016. Southeastern University (NAIA, FL) coaches Richard Sanchez and John Roberts are worked_alongside Southwestern (TX) staff 2020-21. Mark Speckman (Clarion) is worked_alongside Thor Daley (Lincoln Univ., Calif.) at Lincoln University (Pennsylvania). Separately, the exact-match tie-breaker _pick returns ids[0] when an alias is shared. 'Westminster College' goes to Missouri although Matt Hanhold's bio says he was an All-Presidents' Athletic Conference (PAC) player, which is Westminster (PA). 'University of Nevada' goes to UNLV.
evidence: cd /home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline && python3 -I -c "import sys,json; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from resolve import OrgIndex,WORK,ROOT; i=OrgIndex(json.load(open(WORK/'registry.json')),json.load(open(ROOT/'ncaa_members.json'))); [print(r,'->',i.orgs[i.resolve(r,l)]['name']) for r,l in [('Southern Illinois University','NCAA D-I FCS'),('Becker College','NCAA D-III'),('Clarion University of Pennsylvania','NCAA D-II'),('Wesley College','NCAA D-III'),('Taylor University','NAIA'),('Iowa Wesleyan University','unknown'),('Allegany College','unknown'),('Southeastern University','NAIA'),('Tennessee Tech University','NCAA D-I FCS'),('Westminster College','NCAA D-III'),('University of Nevada','NCAA D-I FBS')]]"  prints: Northern Illinois University, Eckerd College, Lincoln University (Pennsylvania), Wellesley College, Baylor University, Ohio Wesleyan University, Allegheny College, Southwestern University (Texas), Tennessee State University, Westminster College (Missouri), University of Nevada, Las Vegas. In data/tree_edges.json: {kind: worked_under, mentorId: p-peter-jennings, menteeId: p-pat-delaney, orgId: ncaa-520, 2009-2009}; {worked_under p-b-j-hammer -> p-mike-deitrick @ Allegheny 2016}; {worked_alongside p-pat-delaney/p-peter-jennings @ Ohio Wesleyan 2008-2010}; 13 Becker College stints sit on Eckerd College (e.g. worked_under p-mike-lichten -> p-frank-forcucci @ Eckerd 2012-2015).
fix: Remove the fuzzy fallback, or accept a fuzzy hit only when the candidate's level matches the stint level, any state hint matches the org's state, and the token sets differ by at most a generic word. Otherwise create an unmatched org. In _pick, return an unresolved/ambiguous org instead of ids[0] when candidates tie.

title: Current-staff tenures without a start year produce no tree edges at all
detail: span() returns None whenever startYear is None, even for isCurrent rows. Being listed on the 2026 staff page proves the person is on that staff in CURRENT_SEASON. 789 of 2,178 current tenures have no startYear, so these people have no edge to their own head coach or colleagues. 675 current assistants at programs whose head coach has a dated current stint have no worked_under edge to that head coach. Re-running resolve with span returning (CURRENT_SEASON, CURRENT_SEASON) for undated current rows yields 2,135 worked_under edges instead of 1,393 (742 more) and 9,423 worked_alongside instead of 4,633 (4,790 more). Also, 59 past coaching tenures with an endYear but no startYear are dropped instead of being treated as a single season.
evidence: Concordia University Wisconsin: HC p-greg-etter (Head Coach, 2008-current) and p-zak-dewindt (current 'Assistant Linebackers Coach...', startYear None). Both are on the staff page, and there are zero edges between them or for DeWindt at that org: python3 -I -c "import json;E=json.load(open('/home/user/klonen_cli/data/tree_edges.json'));print([e for e in E if 'p-zak-dewindt' in (e['mentorId'],e['menteeId'])])" prints []. Rerun with the patched span: scratchpad script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b13a1792-8696-5f9f-a6b8-5bf79408a2f7/scratchpad/resolve_span.py prints edges_worked_under 2135, edges_worked_alongside 9423 (shipped stats.json: 1393 / 4633).
fix: In span(): if s is None and t['isCurrent'], return (CURRENT_SEASON, CURRENT_SEASON). If s is None and endYear is set, use (endYear, endYear).

title: classify() returns 'other' for bare position titles ('Running Backs', 'Defensive Line', ...) and 'other' is excluded from edges
detail: classify() only reaches position_coach when the role contains coach, coordinator or assistant. Titles that name just the position fall through to 'other' even though the unit is detected, as do mixed titles where SUPPORT matches and a unit is set (e.g. 'Cornerbacks / Strength & Conditioning', 'Director of Football Operations/Outside Linebackers', 'Defensive G.A. / Defensive Line'). The edge builder skips roleGroup 'other'. Real data has 607 non-player tenures classified 'other' (230 current), led by Running Backs 52, Wide Receivers 50, Defensive Line 47, Offensive Line 42, Defensive Backs 34, Linebackers 31 and Tight Ends 30. 171 people carry roleGroup 'other'. Mapping ('other', unit!=None) to position_coach and re-running adds 1,462 edges (188 worked_under, 1,274 worked_alongside), and current staff with no edge at their own program fall from 911 to 773.
evidence: python3 -I -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'/home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline');from resolve import classify;print(classify('Wide Receivers',False),classify('Defensive Line',False))" -> ('other','offense') ('other','defense'). St. Olaf (ncaa-615): p-eric-pulley 'Running Backs' (roleGroup other, 2018-current) and HC p-james-kilian (2017-current) have no worked_under edge. The patched rerun (scratchpad run2.py) creates ('worked_under','p-james-kilian','p-eric-pulley','ncaa-615') and 1,461 other missing edges.
fix: In classify, return ('position_coach', unit) whenever a unit was detected and nothing else matched, including when SUPPORT matched alongside a unit, before returning 'other'.

title: Head-coach detection: JV, flag-football, 'interim for two games' and 'consultant to the head coach' count as head coach; real head coaches with 'Assistant/Associate AD' do not
detail: head = regex 'head (football )?coach' AND NOT 'assistant|associate|asst|assoc' anywhere in the string. False positives, each of which becomes mentor of every overlapping assistant: 'Special Teams Coordinator / Junior Varsity Head Coach' (p-hunter-miles, Alfred, 13 edges). Three 'Head Coach, Women's Flag Football' roles plus Cornell College's 'Head Coach (inaugural women's flag football program)' (p-felicia-teeter 14, p-amanda-ruller 6, p-frank-haege 5, p-ralph-clark 2). 'Defensive Coordinator / Linebackers (interim head coach for two games in 2024)' (p-joey-lehto 8). 'Senior Consultant to the Head Coach and Staff' (p-bill-brong, King's 8). In total about 65 fabricated worked_under edges. False negatives: 'Head Coach (also Associate Director of Athletics for External Relations)' becomes support, and 'Head Football Coach / Assistant Athletic Director' becomes position_coach. The worst case is Lakeland University, where the actual head coach Colin Bruton (2015-present) appears as a MENTEE: worked_under p-joey-lehto 2022-2026. He also gets 10 worked_alongside edges with his own assistants instead of worked_under. The classifier also has no sport awareness: 'Head Men's Soccer Coach' (p-angelo-panzetta, Allegheny 2001-2022, 10 edges), 'Head Softball Coach' and 'Offensive Coordinator (men's lacrosse)' all produce football-tree edges. people.json has 5 programs with two head coaches and 2 with none (see F7).
evidence: python3 -I -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'/home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline');from resolve import classify;[print(t,classify(t,False)) for t in ['Junior Varsity Head Coach',\"Head Coach, Women's Flag Football\",'Senior Consultant to the Head Coach and Staff','Defensive Coordinator / Linebackers (interim head coach for two games in 2024)','Head Coach (also Associate Director of Athletics for External Relations)','Head Football Coach / Assistant Athletic Director']]" -> head_coach x4, then support, position_coach. data/tree_edges.json contains {kind: worked_under, mentorId: p-joey-lehto, menteeId: p-colin-bruton, orgId: ncaa-1164, startYear: 2022, endYear: 2026}, and people.json has p-colin-bruton currentTitle 'Head Football Coach'.
fix: Detect head coach on the primary title segment: split on '/', '|', ';' and parentheses. Exclude 'JV|junior varsity|freshman|middle school|junior high|flag football|to the head coach|interim .* for .* games'. Apply the assistant/associate exclusion only when it modifies 'head coach' itself ('assistant head coach', 'associate head coach'), not 'assistant athletic director'. Tag non-football sports (soccer, softball, lacrosse, track, etc.) as 'other' or non-football so they are left out of edges.

title: Current-stint selection uses extraction order: an undated early role becomes current and the real ongoing role is truncated to a single season
detail: is_current goes to the first stint at the program with end in (None, 2026). Later qualifying stints get 'end = end or start', so a dated ongoing role listed after an undated old one (e.g. a 'Student Assistant Coach' from the playing days) is closed at its start year, and the stale role is shown as current. 15 people are affected, and their tree edges for every later season are lost. The corroboration step then sets verified=True on exactly the isCurrent rows (verified == isCurrent for all 8,397 tenures; the cross-bio corroboration in the comment is not implemented), so the wrong row is marked verified.
evidence: Grove City p-dan-vogt (title 'Assistant Football Coach - Defensive Coordinator/Linebackers'). Raw stints: 'Student Assistant Coach' None-None, then 'Defensive Coordinator / Linebackers' 2022-None. Output: current = 'Student Assistant Coach' (None, None, verified True), DC row = 2022-2022 isCurrent False. Same for p-jack-beidler-96 (current 'Special Teams Coordinator' undated; 'Defensive Coordinator (2025-) ... Assistant Head Coach (2026-)' stored 2025-2025) and p-dr-karl-liedtka-91 ('Assistant Coach' undated current; 'Offensive Line Coach / Run Game Coordinator' 2022 stored 2022-2022). Check: python3 -I -c "import json;[print(t['role'],t['startYear'],t['endYear'],t['isCurrent'],t['verified']) for t in json.load(open('/home/user/klonen_cli/data/tenures.json')) if t['personId']=='p-dan-vogt']"
fix: Collect all candidate open stints at the program first. Pick as current the one with the latest startYear, preferring dated over undated and the one matching current_title. Keep other concurrent open stints open (end None or CURRENT_SEASON) rather than truncating them to start. Implement real corroboration or stop setting verified=isCurrent.

verdict.reason:
The finding reproduces. I re-ran pipeline/resolve.py on a scratch copy of pipeline/work/extract and its output matches the committed data/tenures.json, people.json, tree_edges.json and organizations.json byte for byte, so the committed data does come from this code.

Code, pipeline/resolve.py lines 319-324: is_current is set on the first non-player stint at the program whose end is None or 2026. Any later qualifying stint gets is_current=False and `end = end or start`, which closes it at its start year. There is no comparison of start years and no check against current_title.

Raw extract (work/extract/ncaa-265.json, Dan Vogt) lists, in order: 'Student Assistant Coach' None-None, then 'Defensive Coordinator / Linebackers' 2022-None. The output has 'Student Assistant Coach' None/None with isCurrent=True and verified=True, and the DC row as 2022-2022 with isCurrent=False, exactly as the finding says.

That matches the claimed 15 and includes p-dan-vogt, p-jack-beidler-96 and p-dr-karl-liedtka-91. verified == isCurrent holds for all 8,397 tenures. The comment's cross-bio corroboration ("another coach's bio places them there") is not implemented: verified is set only when isCurrent is true at the person's current org.

Dan Vogt's worked_under edge to head coach p-andrew-didonato (current since 2016) stops at 2022 instead of 2026, and Liedtka's only edges are 2022-2022. The feed's new-hires query (isCurrent and startYear == 2026) also misses cases like Michele Braun's 'Head Coach' 2026, which was truncated.

'Every later season lost' does not apply to the 3 cases where the chosen current row is dated (Wheeler, Mueller, Srnka-like); there the current row still spans to 2026. A few of the 15 are arguably concurrent or legitimately past roles, such as Tom Hinkle's 2017 assistant role while he is now head coach. Even so, the selection logic is wrong and produces visible errors on real records: the wrong current role, the wrong row marked verified, and lost edges.

title: robots.txt checked with the full browser-style user agent (bot-specific rules ignored), 5xx/unreachable robots treated as allow-all, robots fetch and 429 not rate-limited
detail: _robots_allows calls rp.can_fetch(UA, url) with UA='Mozilla/5.0 ... CoachGraphResearch/0.1'. urllib.robotparser compares useragent.split('/')[0] = 'mozilla' against each group, so a 'User-agent: CoachGraphResearch' group never applies (and any 'User-agent: Mozilla' group does). Any non-200 robots response, including 5xx, and any network exception sets rp=None, which means allow everything. RFC 9309 requires assuming full disallow when robots.txt is unreachable because of server or network errors. The robots request is not counted in _host_last, so the first page request goes out in the same instant. A 429 response breaks out of the retry loop without honoring Retry-After, and the next request to that host follows 1 second later. Crawl-delay is never read.
evidence: python3 -I -c "import urllib.robotparser as r;UA='Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/124 Safari/537.36 CoachGraphResearch/0.1';p=r.RobotFileParser();p.parse(['User-agent: CoachGraphResearch','Disallow: /']);print(p.can_fetch(UA,'https://x.edu/sports/football/coaches'))" -> True (should be False). Mocked crawl.fetch (scratchpad polite.py, requests.get stubbed, nothing written to cache): host whose robots.txt disallows CoachGraphResearch -> the page is still requested; host whose robots.txt returns 503 -> the page is requested; robots.txt and page both at t=0.0s; 429 with Retry-After: 120 -> the next request to that host goes out at t=1.0s.
fix: Pass a product token, e.g. can_fetch('CoachGraphResearch', url) (or check both the token and '*'). Treat robots 5xx and network errors as disallow (retry later). Update _host_last after the robots fetch. On 429/503, honor Retry-After or back off exponentially. Honor rp.crawl_delay(token) as min_interval.

verdict.reason:
Every technical claim in the finding reproduced, on Python 3.13.16 against /home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline/crawl.py.

1. User-agent matching (line 72, `rp.can_fetch(UA, url)`): `Entry.applies_to` does `useragent.split("/")[0].lower()`, which turns the full browser UA into "mozilla" and then checks whether each group's name is a substring of that.
   - A robots.txt with `User-agent: CoachGraphResearch` / `Disallow: /` still gives `can_fetch(UA, ...)` = True. Calling `can_fetch('CoachGraphResearch', ...)` gives False, as it should.
   - The reverse also holds: a `User-agent: Mozilla` / `Disallow: /` group does apply to this crawler (False).
   - So a site owner who blocks the token the bot advertises in its UA is ignored.
2. Mocked `crawl.fetch`: I stubbed `requests.get` and pointed CACHE at a temp dir, so nothing was written to the repo. The script is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b13a1792-8696-5f9f-a6b8-5bf79408a2f7/scratchpad/f6/polite_check.py.
   - A host whose robots.txt disallows CoachGraphResearch had its page fetched (200).
   - A host whose robots.txt returned 503 had its page fetched. Any non-200 response or RequestException sets `rp=None`, which means allow-all. RFC 9309 says to assume full disallow on 5xx or unreachable.
   - On every host the robots.txt request and the first page request went out at the same instant (t=0.0), because the robots fetch never updates `_host_last`.
   - A 429 with `Retry-After: 120` was followed by the next request to that host at t=1.0s, because `status < 500` breaks the retry loop and Retry-After is never read.
   - A site's `Crawl-delay: 30` was ignored: requests went 1s apart.

This is not negligible:
- The module docstring promises "robots.txt is honoured", and crawl_pass2.py says "we do not work around a site's wishes", but naming this bot in robots.txt has no effect.
- On 429s, `crawl_staff_one` keeps trying the next STAFF_PATH and the bio queue keeps hitting the host at 1 request per second.

The "critical" label is overstated, though; I'd rate it medium to high:
- It is a compliance and politeness bug. It does not corrupt data.
- Real-world exposure from the bot-token mismatch is probably small, since few sites will have a group naming this new token.
- Recorded statuses in pipeline/work/staff.json show 1 robots-disallowed, 27 hosts returning 403 and no 429s. The unreachable hosts (SSLError and ConnectionError) also failed their page fetch, so the allow-all-on-error path did no harm in the run that was done.

title: Renamed schools split into separate orgs: aliases strip 'college'/'university' from official names but resolve() never strips the query
detail: _aliases adds the suffix-stripped core (e.g. 'utica', 'saint john fisher', 'delaware valley', 'manchester', 'heidelberg', 'elmhurst', 'olivet') for each NCAA member. resolve() only looks up the full normalized query. Old names such as 'Utica College', 'St. John Fisher College', 'Delaware Valley College', 'Manchester College', 'Heidelberg College', 'Elmhurst College', 'Olivet College', 'College of Mount St. Joseph', 'Claremont-Mudd-Scripps Colleges' and 'SUNY Buffalo State' therefore become standalone org- entries, all of them registry programs. Stints there are split from the program, and the edges with that program's staff are lost. Example: p-alex-horvatits at 'Utica College' 2017-2019 has no edges with Utica University HC Blaise Faggiano (2008-current) or assistants Matt Rogers, Jerrod Clowes and Tracy Branch. p-anthony-van-curen at 'St. John Fisher College' 2008-2011 is cut off from p-david-blahowicz (SJF 2006-2008, 2010-2015). Unmatched orgs are also keyed only by normalized name, so same-named schools in different states merge: two different 'Portsmouth High School's (RI and Ohio) became one org, producing worked_alongside p-brad-kelly-15 / p-jaylin-kennedy 2019-2021. Kennedy's own evidence says 'Portsmouth (Ohio) High School'. Trivial variants also fragment the same school ('Bluefield College' vs 'Bluefield University', 'Limestone College' vs 'Limestone University', 'Houston Gamblers' vs 'Houston Gamblers (USFL)').
evidence: cd /home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline && python3 -I -c "import sys,json;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from resolve import OrgIndex,WORK,ROOT;i=OrgIndex(json.load(open(WORK/'registry.json')),json.load(open(ROOT/'ncaa_members.json')));print(i.by_norm['utica'], i.orgs[i.by_norm['utica'][0]]['name'], i.resolve('Utica College','NCAA D-III'), i.resolve('St. John Fisher College','NCAA D-III'))" -> ['ncaa-733'] Utica University org-utica-college org-saint-john-fisher-college. data/organizations.json contains both org-utica-college and ncaa-733 (inRegistry true); edge {worked_alongside, p-brad-kelly-15, p-jaylin-kennedy, org-portsmouth-high-school, 2019-2021}.
fix: In resolve(), also try the query with trailing ' college'/' university'/' colleges' removed (and SUNY prefix variants), the same transforms _aliases applies, before creating a new org. Include the stint's state or evidence location in the key for unmatched high schools. Normalize parenthetical league tags off pro team names.

verdict.reason:
The finding reproduces. Two parts need correcting, and the impact is smaller than "major" suggests.

What I checked:
- The evidence command returns ['ncaa-733'] Utica University, org-utica-college, org-saint-john-fisher-college. resolve() (resolve.py:229-262) looks up only the full normalized name and its state-hint variant. The 0.9 fuzzy cutoff does not catch 'utica college' against 'utica'.
- _aliases (lines 208-212) registers the suffix-stripped core, but resolve() never strips the query.
- data/organizations.json has both org-utica-college (inRegistry false) and ncaa-733 (inRegistry true).
- p-alex-horvatits's 2017-2019 'Utica College' stint (extract ncaa-322.json) creates no edge with anyone on ncaa-733: Faggiano (HC 2008-current), Matt Rogers (2016-19), Clowes (2017-), Tracy Branch (2014-20).

Scale: I counted 23 org- college entries whose stripped core matches an NCAA alias. 12 of them map to registry programs, including Olivet, St. John Fisher, Elmhurst, Rockford, Utica, Delaware Valley, Manchester, Heidelberg and Claremont-Mudd-Scripps. SUNY Buffalo State, College of Mount St. Joseph, Bluefield College/University, Limestone College/University and Houston Gamblers / Houston Gamblers (USFL) are all separate orgs, as the finding says.

Portsmouth: the false merge is real. Brad Kelly's Portsmouth High School is in Rhode Island (his extract notes say so). Jaylin Kennedy's evidence says 'Portsmouth (Ohio) High School'. Both resolve to org-portsmouth-high-school, which produces the edge worked_alongside p-brad-kelly-15 / p-jaylin-kennedy 2019-2021.

Corrections:
1. The van Curen example has no edge impact. His St. John Fisher stint is asPlayer=true, and player stints never form edges. Also, Blahowicz's extract already says 'St. John Fisher University', so his stints resolve to ncaa-601.
2. Impact is modest. I merged the 15 genuinely renamed schools into their programs and re-ran the edge build. Edges go from 6026 to 6034, so 8 are missing: 6 at Utica and 2 at Claremont-Mudd-Scripps. The Portsmouth merge adds 1 false edge.
3. Horvatits's role 'JV head coach (2019)' is classified as head_coach. So even after a merge, his recovered edges would come out as worked_under with him as the mentor. That is a separate bug.

Verdict: a real, reproducible correctness bug. Renamed registry schools are split off from their programs, and same-named high schools are merged into one org, which creates a false edge. The severity is closer to moderate than major.

title: Duplicate person: parse_staff accepts link text 'Head Coach' as a name; resolve dedups only by bio_url
detail: The ETBU staff page links the head coach under two bio URLs (/calvin-ruzicka/1086 and /calvin-ruzicka/508). Each has the same two tenures ('Head Coach' 2023-current, 'Defensive Coordinator / Assistant Head Coach' 2018-2022) and duplicate edges (5 each). ETBU shows two head coaches.

title: Edge spans are merged with min/max across separate overlap periods, inventing years of working together
detail: edges[key] = (min(lo, cur[0]), max(hi, cur[1])) merges every overlapping tenure pair into one continuous span. When a person has two separate stints at an org, the edge covers the gap years. 172 edges include at least one season in which the two people never overlapped.
evidence: Franklin College: p-mike-leonard Head Coach 2003-2019 and 2025-current; p-steve-rock 2007-current. Stored edge {worked_under, p-mike-leonard, p-steve-rock, ncaa-2694, 2007, 2026} claims 2020-2024, when Leonard was not there (same for p-bud-boughton). Hendrix: worked_under p-buck-buchanan -> p-noah-simmons 2015-2026, but Simmons' stints there are 2015 and 2023-2026 (gap 2016-2022).
fix: Store a list of (lo, hi) intervals per edge key, or emit one edge row per contiguous overlap interval.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced this one exactly. In /home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline/resolve.py:382 the code runs `edges[key] = (min(lo, cur[0]), max(hi, cur[1])) if cur else (lo, hi)`. That folds every overlapping tenure pair for a (kind, mentor, mentee, org) key into one continuous span, so any years between two separate overlaps get filled in.

Checked against data/tenures.json and data/tree_edges.json:
- **Franklin College (ncaa-2694):** p-mike-leonard has Head Coach tenures 2003-2019 and 2025-current. p-steve-rock and p-bud-boughton both start in 2007 and are current. The stored edges for both are worked_under 2007-2026, which covers 2020-2024, when Leonard was not there.
- **Hendrix (ncaa-1124):** p-noah-simmons has position-coach tenures in 2015 and 2023-current. The edge from p-buck-buchanan to p-noah-simmons is stored as 2015-2026, so the gap years 2016-2022 are claimed.

To check the count I took each edge's tenure pairs, kept the same head-coach and non-head-coach filters the code uses, and compared the union of real overlap years with the stored span. 172 of the 6026 edges claim at least one season with no real overlap, which matches the finding exactly. Of those, 141 are worked_alongside and 31 are worked_under. The invented gaps run from 1 to 13 seasons, and 81 edges claim 3 or more.

This reaches users. web/src/lib/queries/people.ts selects treeEdges.startYear and endYear for display and sorts by endYear, so the person pages show these wrong year ranges. The impact is limited to the year spans: whether the edge exists is still correct, because the two people really did overlap at least once. That makes "major" severity debatable, but the bug is real and shows up on the site.

title: Name parsing keeps class years, generational suffixes and honorifics: wrong lastName/firstName and unstable slugs
detail: fullName is used raw and split on spaces, so lastName becomes the last token. 108 people have lastName equal to a class year or suffix ("'21", "'24G", 'Jr.' x15, 'II', 'III'). Three have firstName 'Dr.'. Slugs and ids embed class years (p-jake-cameron-21, p-tucker-buzzell-24-24g, p-dr-karl-liedtka-91), so ids change if the staff page drops the year.
evidence: python3 -I -c "import json,re;P=json.load(open('/home/user/klonen_cli/data/people.json'));b=[p for p in P if p['lastName'] and re.search(r\"^['’]?\d|^(jr|sr|ii|iii|iv)\.?$\",p['lastName'],re.I)];print(len(b),[(p['fullName'],p['lastName']) for p in b[:4]])" -> 108 [('DeMontre Thomas II','II'), ("Jake Cameron '21","'21"), ("Tucker Buzzell '24, '24G","'24G"), ("Rick Orio '17","'17")]
fix: Strip trailing class-year tokens ("'dd", "'ddG/M", ', DPT ...') and leading honorifics from fullName before slugging. Treat Jr./Sr./II-IV as a suffix rather than lastName.

verdict.reason: The finding reproduces exactly as described. In /home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline/resolve.py (around lines 294-302), the code builds the name with name = re.sub(r"\s+"," ",c["name"]).strip(), then sets slug = slugify(name), firstName = parts[0] and lastName = parts[-1]. It never cleans the name first. Running the evidence query on data/people.json (2178 people) gives exactly 108 bad lastNames. They include Jr. x15, Sr. x2, III x6, II x3, IV x1, Jr x1, and the rest are class years such as '25 x11, '24 x9, '24G and '23M. Three people have firstName 'Dr.': p-dr-eric-calhoun, p-dr-jim-thrasher and p-dr-karl-liedtka-91. 81 fullNames contain a class year, and all 81 have it in the slug and id (for example p-tucker-buzzell-24-24g and p-tim-viall-23m). If the staff page drops the year, the id changes. Impact is real but minor. The web app does not read firstName or lastName yet, though both are stored in the DB schema (web/src/db/schema.ts), so the wrong lastName is a latent data-quality problem. fullName is shown as-is in typeahead and lists, so names like "Tucker Buzzell '24, '24G" appear in the UI and in URLs. Exact-match ranking in web/src/lib/queries/search.ts (lower(fullName) = term) misses these people, but they still match on prefix or substring, so they remain findable. This is a real, persisted data-quality defect, and severity 'minor' is the right label.

title: bio_excerpt picks mid-sentence fragments and non-biographical lines (Bible verses, team stats)
detail: crawl.bio_text uses get_text('\n'), which splits inline tags, so a bolded name ends up on its own line. bio_excerpt takes one line at a time and skips short lines, so the excerpt starts with the verb and drops the subject. 156 of 1,490 excerpts start with a lowercase word. LABEL_LINE only skips lines that end in ':' or start with a fixed label list, so 8 excerpts are 'Favorite Verse: ...' scripture. Others are team-stat paragraphs that never mention the person (e.g. p-ryan-mcelwain, p-zach-riepma).
evidence: data/people.json p-bill-culpepper bioExcerpt 'joined the Cal Lutheran football staff in the fall of 2015 and is the Special Teams Coordinator.'; source file shows '---\nBill Culpepper\njoined the Cal Lutheran...'. p-larry-harmon bioExcerpt 'Favorite Verse: "Have I not commanded you? ..." - Joshua 1:9'.
fix: Join consecutive short lines into paragraphs before choosing (or use get_text(' ') within block elements). Skip lines with an inline 'Label:' prefix (e.g. Favorite Verse). Require that the excerpt mention the person's first or last name, or start with a pronoun after one that does.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced it. In data/people.json, 1,490 people have a bioExcerpt. 156 of them start with a lowercase word and 8 are "Favorite Verse:" scripture lines, which matches the finding's numbers exactly. p-bill-culpepper's excerpt is "joined the Cal Lutheran football staff in the fall of 2015...". In the cached HTML the bio is written as `

Bill Culpepper joined the Cal Lutheran...`. crawl.bio_text calls get_text(" ", strip=True), which puts the bolded name on its own line, and the bio file confirms this ("--- Bill Culpepper joined..."). bio_excerpt in pipeline/resolve.py skips any line under 90 characters, so it drops the name and quotes the predicate on its own. LABEL_LINE only matches its fixed list of label prefixes or a line ending in ":", so "Favorite Verse: "..." - Joshua 1:9" gets through (p-larry-harmon). The excerpts for p-ryan-mcelwain and p-zach-riepma are team-stat paragraphs that never name the person. I re-ran bio_excerpt over every current bio file with the current code and got the same pattern (1,514 excerpts, 165 lowercase starts, 9 verses), so this is not a stale output file. Impact: design/feature-briefs.json says the profile About card shows bioExcerpt as a verbatim quote, "Quoted from the staff bio", whenever person.about is empty, and the brief notes that field is usually empty. About 10% of profiles would therefore show a sentence fragment with no subject, a Bible verse, or team stats as the coach's About. The web UI does not render the field yet (it appears only in schema.ts), so "minor" is the right severity, but the defect is real and visible.

title: crawl_pass2's widened bio-link pattern never takes effect because parse_staff only selects a[href*='/coaches/']
detail: crawl_pass2 sets crawl.COACH_LINK = EXTRA_LINK to accept /staff-directory/<name>/<id> links. Hiram (ncaa-281) and SUNY Morrisville (ncaa-30067) end up 'no-staff-parsed-pass2' even though their cached pages have 76 and 59 staff-directory links. title: Validator does not enforce one coach object per bio; resolve then silently keeps the first duplicate
detail: The docstring promises 'exactly one coach object' per bio, but main() only adds URLs to a seen set and never flags a second object with the same bio_url. resolve.main skips later objects via seen_urls, so if the extractor emitted a corrected second object it is dropped without warning.
evidence: Copy work/extract/ncaa-38.json, append a second object with the same bio_url (different name, empty stints), save as scratchpad vtest/ncaa-38.json, run python3 -I /home/user/klonen_cli/pipeline/validate_extract.py vtest/ncaa-38.json -> 'ncaa-38.json: 14 coaches, 67 stints, 0 problems', exit 0.
fix: In validate_extract, report 'duplicate coach object for bio <url>' when url is already in seen. In resolve, log or raise on duplicate bio_url instead of skipping silently.

verdict.reason: The finding reproduces, but nothing in the current data triggers it. I copied work/extract/ncaa-38.json and added a 14th object that reuses the first object's bio_url (kijuan-ware/2614), with name 'Corrected Name' and empty stints. title: Org kind/level don't match the name or the NCAA football list
detail:
Kind or level wrong for the name:
- org-united-states-military-academy-army-west-point is kind high_school with level 'NCAA D-I FBS'. It is also a duplicate of ncaa-725.
- 13 high schools have level None. Some aren't high schools at all: the state athletic association (MHSAA), a recruiting service (NHR Prospects), a youth academy (Eagles), sports-training academies, and junior highs. Meanwhile 8 middle schools are kind 'other', so younger schools are handled inconsistently.
- Pro orgs that aren't football: Lehigh Valley IronPigs (minor-league baseball) and 'Professional indoor and outdoor soccer'.
- 3 football leagues or teams are kind 'other'.
- 16 colleges have level None, including the placeholder 'Unspecified college football staffs'.
- 2 placeholders carry level 'NCAA D-III' ('Unnamed UMAC school', 'Unknown (Landmark Conference school...)').

Level vs pipeline/ncaa_mfb.json: 8 ncaa-* levels disagree.
- Two are programs in the D-III list that pick up current staff: ncaa-30146 Azusa Pacific is labelled D-II (11 current staff) and ncaa-600 Saint Francis is labelled D-I FCS (9 current staff). That is 20 staff on 'D-III' programs that the data says are not D-III.
- The others: ncaa-102 FCS vs FBS, ncaa-493 FCS vs FBS, ncaa-408, ncaa-470, ncaa-766 (D-II vs FCS), ncaa-225 (D-III vs D-II).

Also: 11 non-football Division I schools have the vague level 'NCAA D-I'; 4 duplicate pairs disagree on level (F2); 2 names have trailing spaces (ncaa-525, ncaa-600); and no org-* id (1,464) has a state, which blocks state-based disambiguation.
evidence:
Regex on the name compared with kind/level, then levels joined to ncaa_mfb.json by ncaaOrgId (division and subdivision).
- org-united-states-military-academy-army-west-point: kind high_school, level NCAA D-I FBS
- org-michigan-high-school-athletic-association and org-national-high-school-recruiting-prospects-nhr-prospects: kind high_school, level None
- org-lehigh-valley-ironpigs: kind pro, level pro/semi-pro
- ncaa-30146 Azusa Pacific: level NCAA D-II, inRegistry true, ncaa_mfb division 3
fix: Set kind and level from rules: NCAA or service-academy names become college with the level from ncaa_mfb; middle and junior high go to one 'youth' kind; associations, recruiting services and training businesses become 'other'; non-football pro teams are dropped. Refresh ncaa-* levels from ncaa_mfb.json on every bundle. Trim names. Fill state for org-* ids from the evidence where possible.

verdict.reason:
The core of the finding reproduces, and part of it shows up for users. data/organizations.json has 2097 orgs: 633 ncaa-* and 1464 org-*.

**ncaa-* levels vs pipeline/ncaa_mfb.json.** I joined on ncaaOrgId with the same division/subdivision mapping as resolve.py's level_of. Exactly 8 disagree:
- ncaa-30146 Azusa Pacific: D-II, but mfb says D-III
- ncaa-600 Saint Francis: D-I FCS, but mfb says D-III
- ncaa-102 Sacramento State and ncaa-493 North Dakota State: FCS, but mfb says FBS
- ncaa-408 Mercyhurst, ncaa-470 New Haven and ncaa-766 West Georgia: D-II, but mfb says FCS
- ncaa-225 Ferrum: D-III, but mfb says D-II

The cause is in pipeline/resolve.py: OrgIndex sets levels from ncaa_members.json, which still has the old divisions. It never reads the football-specific ncaa_mfb.json.

**User impact.** Azusa Pacific and Saint Francis are both in the 244-program D-III registry (inRegistry true). They carry 11 and 9 current staff. That makes them the only non-D-III current orgs in people.json (2158 D-III, 11 D-II, 9 FCS). The product spec says it is "launching with NCAA Division III football". Yet web/src/lib/queries/search.ts filters by division with `eq(organizations.level, f.division)`. So choosing "NCAA D-III" hides those 20 coaches. facetOptions() also lists stray "NCAA D-II" and "NCAA D-I FCS" options that contain only these two programs.

**Other sub-claims that check out:**
- org-united-states-military-academy-army-west-point is kind high_school with level NCAA D-I FBS. It duplicates ncaa-725 (U.S. Military Academy).
- 13 high_school orgs have level None. They include the Michigan High School Athletic Association, NHR Prospects, the Philadelphia Eagles Youth Academy, two junior highs and sports academies.
- 8 middle schools are kind 'other'.
- The pro orgs include Lehigh Valley IronPigs and "Professional indoor and outdoor soccer".
- 16 colleges have level None, including "Unspecified college football staffs".
- "Unnamed UMAC school" and "Unknown (Landmark Conference school...)" are both labelled NCAA D-III.
- 11 orgs have the bare level "NCAA D-I".
- ncaa-525 and ncaa-600 have trailing spaces in their names.
- None of the 1464 org-* ids has a state.

**Caveats.** Most org-* problems touch only 1 to 3 tenures each. The "NCAA D-I" label is accurate for those schools, so calling it vague is a nitpick. The count of "3 football teams kind other" understates the real number. These don't refute the finding. The level mismatch alone breaks a visible filter and mislabels two in-scope programs.

title: Tree edges pass the overlap check, but 60 pairs carry both edge kinds for the same years and 14 sit at wrong orgs
detail:
Clean checks:
- All 6,026 edges have both years set. Each edge's year range lies inside both people's coaching (non-player) intervals at that org, so non-overlapping edges: 0.
- Self-edges by id: 0; dangling references: 0; exact duplicates: 0.
- In every worked_under edge, the mentor held a head_coach stint in that period.
- How many mentors a mentee has: 1 for 878 people, 2 for 180, 3 for 41, 4 for 8. No head coach has even 5 mentors, so the 'dozens of mentors' pattern does not occur. The most mentees any mentor has is 20 (p-brant-mcadams).

Problems:
- 213 pairs at the same org have both a worked_under and a worked_alongside edge; in 60 of them the years overlap. An example is a one-year interim head coach whose colleagues are both 'under' and 'alongside' him for the same season.
- 3 pairs have worked_under edges in both directions at one org, in different years. These are role reversals, not errors.
- 1 effective self-edge comes from the duplicate person (F6).
- 14 edges are anchored at schools that don't play football, from the F1 wrong matches.
evidence:
Overlapping under + alongside pairs:
- (p-ryan-mcelwain, p-steve-rock, ncaa-2694): worked_under 2019-2019, worked_alongside 2018-2023
- (p-ryan-mcelwain, p-bud-boughton, ncaa-2694): worked_under 2019-2019, worked_alongside 2018-2023
- (p-scott-srnka, p-brett-dietz, ncaa-177): worked_under 2012-2012, worked_alongside 2011-2019
Edges at a wrong org: worked_under p-mike-lichten to p-mark-theophel, ncaa-208 (Eckerd), 2011
fix: When building worked_alongside, leave out the years in which one person was head coach over the other, or split the edge into separate year ranges. Rebuild edges after the F1, F2 and F6 fixes. Add tests in pipeline/test_resolve.py for both-kinds overlap and same-person edges.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced it against data/tree_edges.json and resolve.py, and every number checks out. There are 6,026 edges. None is missing years, none is a self-edge by id, none dangles, and none is an exact duplicate. 213 directed pairs at the same org have both a worked_under and a worked_alongside edge (212 if the pairs are unordered). In exactly 60 of those, the year ranges overlap. The 878/180/41/8 split reproduces exactly, but it counts worked_under edges per mentee, not distinct mentors as the finding says; counting distinct mentors gives 885/175/40/7. The top mentor is p-brant-mcadams with 20 mentees. There are 3 role reversals (under edges in both directions). All example edges exist as quoted. One small difference: the Lichten-to-Theophel edge runs 2011-2013, not just 2011. There are 14 edges at ncaa-208 Eckerd College, which has no football team; they all come from Becker College being matched to Eckerd, so they belong to F1. One more edge sits at Northeastern, which dropped football in 2009, so it may be correct history.

The cause is in resolve.py around lines 363-382. The code merges every tenure a person has at an org. So when someone holds a head_coach stint and a non-head-coach stint there with overlapping years, it produces both edge kinds for the same pair and years. The UI then lists the same person as both a mentor and a peer for the same years (getTree in web/src/lib/queries/people.ts puts each kind in its own list).

The finding's main example, an interim head coach, is the weakest case. Only 12 of the 60 involve an interim head coach. McElwain was defensive coordinator most of 2019 and interim head coach only for November-December, so at year granularity both edges are arguably true. The other 48 are clearer errors:
- **Women's flag football head coaches (21 of 60):** classified as head_coach for the football program, so they become the football staff's boss. Felicia Teeter alone accounts for 14; Haege and R. Clark make up the rest.
- **Athletic-department roles counted as peers:** Mike Clark's Director of Athletics stint gives him worked_alongside edges for 2012-2025 with assistants who were under him as head coach. Rehring's assistant AD role does the same.
- **Odd mixed roles:** C.C. Grant and Catanzaro have strange role combinations.

So the problem is real and visible on profiles, but small: 60 of 6,026 edges, about 1%. Minor severity fits. The finding gets the main cause wrong, though: it is mostly roles classified wrongly, not interim stints.
